jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis puts the number in his phone. You never know.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The flyer is already in your pocket. The board looks relieved.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Something about it is off: its battery pack looks a lot like a handheld scanner battery, held in with electrical tape and confidence.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The clock reads 9:02. It has read 9:02 for as long as anyone can remember, which the break room finds comforting.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis lifts the clock off its nail and pops out the taped-in battery. It is, in fact, a scanner battery.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The clock is now a decorative circle. It is at peace.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Already open, already empty.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A couch that has absorbed a decade of lunch breaks, three union meetings and, allegedly, a nap by Torvald that lasted through a shift change.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Something metallic glints between the cushions.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis checks the cushions like a professional. He finds two quarters, a pen cap, and a tiny sock. Two quarters go in his pocket.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Nothing else in the cushions but structural regret.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: From somewhere behind it comes a faint chirp. Radio-like. Ashamed.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Slot D4 is glowing. Softly. Minty. A sign says "PLEASE ENJOY."

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A vending machine with the ambition of a small vending machine. One slot, D4, is empty except for a warm blink.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A gap behind the vending machine, about the width of a dog and a half. Something in there is blinking green.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A gap. Empty now. Hollis is a little proud of the dog.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Juno wedges into the gap. There is a clatter, a beep, and a muffled complaint.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Juno has already been a hero here.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis takes the bowl. Several sets of eyes track the bowl as it leaves.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: You are out of quarters.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis already has a bag of crackers. Quarters are not infinite. He keeps his hands in his pockets.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: You press D4. The machine hums a note that does not exist. A single mint tumbles into the tray, glowing with the calm confidence of something that has never been audited.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis looks at the mint. Every instinct says no. It hums, faintly, like something the building has been hiding. Not yet.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: If this ends up in a report, I want it noted that I was reasonable.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: I have no idea what this is.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Juno, sitting beside him, tilts her head.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis stares at the glowing mint. Company policy has opinions about this.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: It tastes like a cold winter morning and a fresh spreadsheet.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The warehouse lighting flickers, all at once. Every scanner in the building reboots. Labels flutter off pallets and into the air like startled birds.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Every cat in the room turns to look at Hollis, at the same instant. It is not a look that comes with a comfortable explanation.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis can see it now. Above every pallet, a tag of routing data. Above every forklift, an identity. Above the floor, a lattice of freight flow, dotted with cats that follow it like sheepdogs. The world is a system, and he can read it.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis is back where he left off.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Click. Nope. The lock rolls its eyes.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Click. No. Hollis has no idea what the numbers are. Someone, somewhere, wrote them down.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Click. Also no. The lock was not born yesterday.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Click! The numbers on the back of that label were right.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The locker swings open. Inside: a pen, and a cell phone with 4% battery, both exactly where Hollis would have put them.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Open. The interior smells like work boots and possibility.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis takes the pen and his phone.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A combination lock. Three numbers. Hollis stares at it like a man who has forgotten his own PIN, because he has.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Locker 114. Yours, in theory. The padlock hangs open, and the dent still looks intentional.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Locker 114. Yours, in theory. It has a combination padlock and a dent that looks intentional.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Already open. Nothing else in there but pine-scented resignation.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Inside: seven hi-vis vests, a thermos, a sleeping bag, and a single work glove that smells strongly of tobacco and pine.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Just splinters.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A quarter has been lodged in the seam.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A long bench with worn boot scuffs.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis pries a quarter out of the seam with a fingernail. Modest, but real.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The Lost & Found box. It contains a single boot, a Bluetooth speaker that plays only static, and a folded pink blanket that has clearly been thoroughly loved. A tally counter peeks from underneath.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The Lost & Found box. A single boot and a Bluetooth speaker that plays only static. The blanket and the tally counter are gone.

jobs.speaker: PRUDENCE
jobs.tts_text: Oh, I can't accept things. I'm not technically on the payroll. But put it on the bench.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: PRUDENCE — Employment status: TERMINATED. Location: HERE. Badge: EXPIRED, functional. Task: "just finishing something". Task duration: 11 weeks.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The HR door is closed. A sticky note: "Back at 9:02." It has been 9:02 in HR for about a year.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A cushion-tire forklift, unmistakable to anyone who has ever touched one: solid tires, low seat, no propane tank, a dent in the guard that Hollis has personal history with. The plate says F-2231.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: A record that is wrong is a reason. Ingrid keeps saying she needs one of those before she touches the paperwork. This might be it.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: It's right there.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The warehouse computer says this forklift is currently in Tennessee.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The computer remains confident.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: F-2231 — Type per plate: CUSHION-TIRE, serial CT-2231. Type per system: PROPANE SIT-DOWN. Location per system: TENNESSEE.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: F-2231 — CUSHION-TIRE. System agrees. Location: HERE. The scanner sounds almost smug.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The HALO regional dashboard, mounted on the wall like a saint. Every bar is green. Every number is 100%. Below it, a cat is sitting on a shelf, indifferent to metrics.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: It has never once been correct and has never once been red.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis takes the bowl. A dozen cats stare. One of them says something rude in cat.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: TUCKER — Enthusiasm: 100%. Competence:, loading.... Loyalty: OVERFLOW. Warning: this employee has been scanned into fourteen wrong locations.

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: Oh! Is this for me?! I mean, I'll hold it! I'll... hold it!

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The trailer assignment board. Door 3: T-9022, READY. Doors 2 and 6: the two inbound trailers, "UNLOADED*". The asterisk is doing an enormous amount of work.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The trailer assignment board. Door 3: T-9022, AT DOOR. For the first time today, the board is telling the truth.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The trailer assignment board. Door 3: T-9022, DEPARTED. Someone has drawn a tiny trailer driving off the edge of the board.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Someone who is technically not here.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: I believe so.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: Ah.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: ...Is this the last decent coffee?

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: Who had it?

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: She already has coffee. She's not greedy. She just needs it.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Ingrid drinks. Something in the room relaxes by about four degrees.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: It needs a signature from Operations. That's literally the point of the form.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: It's blank. That's a piece of paper, not a request.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: Form 7-Q, filled, signed. Where did you find a pen? I'm genuinely impressed.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: It says nothing is wrong yet. Scan something that is wrong and come back.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: Cushion-tire, per the plate. Propane, per the system. Tennessee, per the system. And it is standing forty feet from my desk.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: ...Fine. That is a reason. I will note it.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: If it creates work, no.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Ingrid's eyes rise slowly from her work and meet yours over the top of her monitor. Hollis takes his hand off the mouse.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Ingrid's WMS terminal. A sticky note on the screen: "IF YOU TOUCH THIS I WILL KNOW". Hollis respects the sticky note.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis holds the crumpled label up to the terminal. The terminal makes a noise like a very small door closing. Nothing else happens. Yet.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: There's always a cat on my paperwork. He's been there since Friday. He's a coworker now.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Ingrid's desk. It is a stable ecosystem of manifests, bills of lading, sticky notes, and one small orange cat asleep on a stack of shipping papers.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Ingrid's terminal, the WMS, warehouse management system: the computer that claims to know where everything is. Guest access. The screen offers "TRAILERS", "ASSETS" and "DIRECTIVES, LOCKED".

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: For once, it is.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: For once, the computer and the parking lot agree.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: There is an empty trailer at door 3 in the computer. There is not one at door 3 in real life. The computer is completely sure.

jobs.speaker: SYSTEM
jobs.tts_text: T-4418 — INBOUND, DOOR 6, 8 loads, status: RECONCILED.

jobs.speaker: SYSTEM
jobs.tts_text: T-4417 — INBOUND, DOOR 2, 8 loads, status: RECONCILED.

jobs.speaker: SYSTEM
jobs.tts_text: T-9022 — OUTBOUND, DOOR 3, status: READY.

jobs.speaker: SYSTEM
jobs.tts_text: T-9022 — OUTBOUND, DOOR 3, EMPTY, status: READY.

jobs.speaker: SYSTEM
jobs.tts_text: T-9022 — DEPARTED 11:59, 8 loads, seal 88120.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The screen and the floor finally agree.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Nothing on the screen agrees with anything outside it.

jobs.speaker: SYSTEM
jobs.tts_text: F-2231 — PROPANE SIT-DOWN — location: TENNESSEE.

jobs.speaker: SYSTEM
jobs.tts_text: RT-77 — REACH TRUCK — location: REMOTE SITE.

jobs.speaker: SYSTEM
jobs.tts_text: LOADS A3, A4 — REACH TRUCKS — dest: NEBRASKA, per Directive 7-C.

jobs.speaker: SYSTEM
jobs.tts_text: RT-77 — CUSHION-TIRE — location: REMOTE SITE.

jobs.speaker: SYSTEM
jobs.tts_text: F-2231 — CUSHION-TIRE — location: HERE.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Good morning.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: Is it? You have a cat on your... no, that's a shadow. What do you need?

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Ingrid has the tired, patient look of a woman who has been asked, in the last hour, for six things that are not her job.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Is it?

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: The WMS also says F-2231 is in Tennessee. I've stopped reading the WMS aloud.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: The WMS finally agrees F-2231 is here. It's unsettling.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: Kestrel Motor Works. PO 55-1187. Eight lines. T-9022 to Door 3. The WMS says it's all in place and ready.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: I'm not being difficult. If I do everyone's job, then it stops being a job and starts being a hostage situation.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: ...Coffee. A signed 7-Q. A scan of a forklift that's in two places. [pause] You did the work first. That's so rare I almost cried.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Ingrid hits print. The printer wakes. A packet slides out: T-4417 and T-4418 manifests, page 1. Then she pauses.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: Page two of the 4417 manifest is missing. It disappeared Friday. Last seen near a cat.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: Also, here. Guest login for the WMS terminal: read-only. Don't break it. And here are the phone numbers: Gordon at Kestrel. Ozzie at the remote site. They're both very... available.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: Page 2. Lines 5 through 8. If it turns up... I'd prefer it wasn't chewed. It was last on a cat. I'm told the cat is orange, and answers to a rank.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: You have it? That's the only accurate document in the building. Put a note on it.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: They're coworkers now. There's one on my paperwork. He's not a problem. He's a stakeholder.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: I've accepted the cats. Some of them are better at the job than the people I trained.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: Page 1. Page 2. Decoded lines. Fixed identities. Sorted staging. I think we can make a true bill of lading.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: That's the first piece of paperwork I have printed this month that I am proud of.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Ingrid prints it. It slides out cleanly. She holds it up to the light like a proud parent.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: It approved its own directive.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: And then it thanked itself for its service.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis has traced the chaos upward: Operations followed the system, the system followed a Regional directive, and the Regional directive followed the system. It is a circle. It is a perfectly green circle.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Below the directive, another line — the identity swap. Below THAT, a metric labeled "Cats" pointing at nothing at all.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: With MINT vision, the dashboard's glow peels back like a wet label. Lines of routing data run up out of it to the ceiling. Hollis follows one.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: HALO DASHBOARD — Accuracy: 100%. Physical inventory match: 0 of 16. Warehouse cats: N/A. Note: this device is not used to being asked questions.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: HALO DASHBOARD — Accuracy: 100%. Physical inventory match: 16 of 16. The dashboard reports 100% either way. Warehouse cats: N/A.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: It's signed. Go. GO.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: It's blank. I can't approve nothing. Actually I can. But I won't.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: A 7-Q? For Ingrid?...Fine. What's the reason?

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: Approved. Don't tell Regional I approved a form. We're not measured on forms.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: I don't have time for that. Or for anything.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Hot shipment.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The Ops printer. A single sheet sits in the tray. It says FORM 7-Q: INFORMATION ACCESS REQUEST, For requests that will create work for Shipping, please submit for Approval.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The tray is empty. It is already regretting.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The Ops printer. The tray is empty. It hums like it is already printing the next problem.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: It left. On time. 11:59. I'm still sitting down.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: The hot shipment. Yes. Kestrel. Noon. Regional has flagged it. I can't stress that enough. I'm already stressed. Please go make it happen.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: Regional Director Harrow. Very focused on numbers. Very supportive of an accurate dashboard. She calls every hour, on the hour, to check whether the dashboard is right. It always is.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: Who told you about... nobody is supposed to... it's a Regional directive. I don't write them. I just... follow what the system says. And the system says what Regional says. And Regional...

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: Please stop making it a circle.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Says what the system says.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: It's just the dashboard. It's always green. It's green right now.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Dale. I need to understand where the directives came from.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis needs more than a green dashboard. There's a way to see through it. MINT vision, on the dashboard.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: It thanked itself? It does that.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: It was on time? The system said it was on time. [pause] It said it was on time all week.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: The system approved its own directive at 4:07 Friday morning. Directive 7-C. Then it thanked itself.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Dale. It's over. The load went out. Right pallets, right trailer, right time.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The shipment has left. The trailer is gone. The cats are safe. Halvorsen is at his desk, holding a phone that isn't ringing.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: I've been doing what it says for two years. Every directive. Every shortfall. It moved things. I moved things. Regional wanted the numbers to match. So I made the warehouse match the numbers. [pause] Hollis... I'm sorry. I didn't know the cats were real.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: I know, Dale.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The conflict appears to end here, with Operations. It does not.

jobs.speaker: HARROW
jobs.tts_text: Good noon. I'm Constance Harrow, Regional Director. I'm told the hot shipment departed. Congratulations. That's a 100% on-time load rate. For the quarter, that's a 100.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Every monitor in the office flickers to a shade of green Hollis has never seen. The dashboard on the wall reforms itself into a single video panel.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A woman in a navy blazer appears on screen, seated in front of a beautiful, terrifying, perfect chart.

jobs.speaker: HARROW
jobs.tts_text: Regional Operational Review. Regional Operations Suite. Fifteen minutes. Hollis, please bring your data. If you have any.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: Hollis. She takes the reviews seriously. Bring... everything.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The screen goes dark. The dashboard reads "ALL GREEN".

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Prudence is suddenly standing in the doorway, holding a cup. She has been there the whole time.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Where's the entrance?

jobs.speaker: PRUDENCE
jobs.tts_text: You'll want to go up. The stairs are Gus's. He won't let you through. But the cats have been using Conveyor 9 since Friday. It goes to a server closet. Regional never checks the server closet.

jobs.speaker: PRUDENCE
jobs.tts_text: Rack 14. Ask Juno. She already knows.

jobs.speaker: TABITHA
jobs.tts_text: I'm not authorized to receive that, but I can note that you tried.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: It's not 9:02.

jobs.speaker: TABITHA
jobs.tts_text: It's always 9:02 in PolicyPilot. Can you just breathe on the sensor?

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis breathes. The tablet screen flickers, goes cyan, goes green, goes a color that is a little bit like sound.

jobs.speaker: TABITHA
jobs.tts_text: That's... that's new.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The door opens. Four cats stroll in. Then eight. They sit in a semicircle around Hollis, observing him with respect and, faintly, accountability.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Juno watches the whole thing from the doorway. Her expression is a formal statement of judgment.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Great. Can I go?

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Tabitha taps at the tablet with a small, brave, HR smile.

jobs.speaker: TABITHA
jobs.tts_text: I can't let you go with no paperwork. It would be... a hole. We'll do an exemption. Form 9-M: "Exemption for Non-Standard Breath". It's new. I'm writing it now.

jobs.speaker: TABITHA
jobs.tts_text: Okay. I'm searching for the policy on supernatural breath mints. Searching... Searching... [pause] There is no policy.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Tabitha stamps a form with a heartfelt thunk, then stamps it again for luck.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Does the Safety Committee have any openings?

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Juno barks once. Tabitha looks at her. Tabitha looks at the form. Tabitha looks at Juno.

jobs.speaker: TABITHA
jobs.tts_text: ...She's very qualified.

jobs.speaker: TABITHA
jobs.tts_text: One vacancy. There are no requirements. It's a temp position. Do you know someone?

jobs.speaker: TABITHA
jobs.tts_text: Anything else I can help with? I have a lot of forms.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Rows and rows of small parts bins labeled with codes only the Parts Department understands, and, at night, the Parts Department's ghost. One label reads "H-17 — HYDRAULIC SEALS, PALLET JACK, MISC".

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The bin is empty. The donut remains.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: It is locked and there is nothing in there Hollis needs.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The maintenance cage: torque wrenches, drum keys, one very brave mop. Neatly locked. Neatly.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The padlock needs the cage key. Hollis is looking at a lock designed by a person who did not anticipate Tucker.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The maintenance cage. The door is padlocked from the OUTSIDE. Tucker is on the inside, waving through the bars with the enthusiasm of a man on a parade float.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The cage is locked and nobody is in it. Hollis keeps the key. He has a feeling.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: It is already unlocked. Tucker got out the way Tucker gets out of things: eventually.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: It does not help. The cage is a cage. The lock is a lock.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: BANG. BANG. BANG. A rhythmic, cheerful sound is coming from the maintenance cage.

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: HI HOLLIS! I'M FINE! I JUST HAD TO LET THE CATS OUT OF THE SECURED AREA AND THEN THE DOOR LOCKED! BUT THEY'RE OUT! ALL OF THEM! [pause]...THEY'RE ALL IN HERE NOW ACTUALLY.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The hook is empty. Its sign still says "SEE TUCKER".

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Empty hook. Not empty of meaning.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A hook labeled "CAGE KEY — DO NOT LOSE". A key hangs from it. Below, a sign: "IF KEY IS MISSING SEE TUCKER." The key is not missing, which is exciting.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Rack 14. The bottom two levels are empty except for shadow. Cats keep walking into this gap, one after another, with purpose. None come out. It is a very organized disappearance.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Rack 14: behind the pallet wall, an old conveyor tunnel. The cats knew.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Juno noses along the base of the rack. A pallet that looked bolted down is just leaning. She shoulders it. Behind it: a dark opening, and a cat-shaped silhouette sitting in it like a doorman.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR

jobs.tts_text: Hollis collects the third bowl. He feels like he has just closed a very small door on a very big problem.

jobs.tts_text: The staging board now reads CLEAR. Someone has drawn a small, smug cat next to it.

jobs.tts_text: A cat is sitting in the doorway, not moving. Closing it would be theft of a cat's front door. It may be best to solve the actual problem first.

jobs.tts_text: Hollis rolls door 9 shut. It closes with a satisfying WHUMP. The last of the outside comes to an end.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: It is shut. It is done.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Dock door 9, ROLLED UP since who-knows-when. The seal is torn. There is a line of paw prints leading in from the yard and a second line, much smaller, leading in behind them.

jobs.tts_text: Not a loader thing. What do you need?

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Door 3. T-9022 is finally in it, doors open, dock plate down, and the light is green. It is a pretty sight.

jobs.tts_text: The trailer is seated. Pushing it would be a strange way to celebrate.

jobs.tts_text: The dock door is up. It does not need to be pushed. It needs a trailer.

jobs.tts_text: I'm standing here. It's dock 3. I'm holding a radio. I'm being a spotter. Don't make it weird.

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: Before I go stand somewhere useful. Here.

jobs.tts_text: Everyone needs the hot shipment. I need a jack that works. It leaks. Ask me about it, then we'll talk.

jobs.tts_text: Hollis. Good, you're upright. What do you need?

jobs.tts_text: The hot shipment.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: If you could find me an H-17, I'd tell you things. Useful things.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: Leaking seal. Been that way since March. Parts hasn't had the H-17 in stock. Parts hasn't had anyone in Parts in a month.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: What was supposed to load: eight pallets to Kestrel. Where they are: staging. Where the staging lanes are: full of inbound freight from two trailers. Sixteen pallets total.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: Nothing. That's the problem. Friday, the dashboard told me to load two reach trucks to Nebraska. There's no Nebraska on my dock. I didn't load them. Then it told me the trailer was ready. It wasn't here.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: I mark the pallets I've checked. It makes sense to me. [pause] Fix my jack and I'll tell you what it means.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: Orange dot: goes on my truck. Blue dot: stays inside. No dot: I didn't touch it. Usually a cat, or a label I didn't like.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: I don't load a pallet with a cat on it. It's a rule. It's my rule. It's a good one.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: One pallet in staging has twelve on it. Warm. I'm not touching that until they choose to leave.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: Halvorsen says Regional says the dashboard is right. Regional says Halvorsen says the same. It's a nice circle. I stay out of it. I load trucks.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: Staging clear, trailer at the door, cats off my pallets. Simple. Sorting is your part. Loading is mine.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: I don't close a trailer without a bill of lading. Ingrid knows. And Kestrel and the remote site have to have signed off.

jobs.speaker: RUFUS
jobs.tts_text: T-9022 is rolling. I can see the dock. I can't see the light. Torvald?

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: I'm looking at the light. It's red. It's yellow. Wait. Hollis, you call it.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: I need

jobs.speaker: GORDON

jobs.tts_text: Eight loads shipped. Eight loads stored. The staging lanes are empty. The scanners agree with the racks. The manifest balances.

jobs.tts_text: It has bowls and bedding. It is, actually, kind of nice.

jobs.tts_text: Hollis fishes a quarter out of the frame with a fingernail. A cat watches him with what looks like professional curiosity.

jobs.tts_text: There is a quarter lodged in the grate's frame.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Nothing else but cold water and moral complications.

jobs.tts_text: Oh, put it down, please. I would rather not be technically in possession. I don't want to be technically in possession.

jobs.tts_text: The reader stays red. Gus doesn't move. The only other way in is not through Gus.

jobs.tts_text: There is no leaving during a Regional Review.

jobs.tts_text: The trailer backs six feet, corrects itself, and returns to the yard with dignity.

jobs.speaker: RUFUS
jobs.tts_text: Again.

jobs.tts_text: T-9022 eases into Door 3. The dock plate falls with a satisfying clang. The light is green. The computer, for the first time in a week, is correct. It has no idea why.

jobs.speaker: RUFUS
jobs.tts_text: GO. Backing in. Torvald, call it.

jobs.tts_text: ...Come on back. Come back. Keep coming. Aaand STOP.

jobs.tts_text: The dashboard redefines a metric while Hollis hesitates. Reality frays at the edges.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: HALO rewrites the records faster than Hollis can read. The numbers reset. He inhales. He tries again.

jobs.speaker: HARROW
jobs.tts_text: This is a Regional Operational Review. I'd like to begin by saying: everything is functioning at a hundred percent. The dashboard tells me so. I would ask you to demonstrate otherwise. Take your time. Not too much.

jobs.speaker: HARROW
jobs.tts_text: You came through the server closet.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: I took the scenic route.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Constance Harrow stands at the head of the conference table, tablet in hand. Behind her, the HALO wall shines with a serene, perfect, all-green light. Juno sits beside Hollis. Juno's armband glows faintly.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The suite hums. Somewhere, a fan starts.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The walls of the suite begin to shudder. Labels flutter down from the ceiling. The HALO wall reassigns something with a tiny, cheerful ding.

jobs.speaker: HARROW

jobs.speaker: HARROW
jobs.tts_text: The dashboard is never wrong. That's the whole point of the dashboard. If it's wrong, then everything it has reported —

jobs.speaker: HARROW
jobs.tts_text: ...The dashboard says the numbers have not changed.

jobs.tts_text: —was reported by a dashboard.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: The dashboard is wrong.

jobs.speaker: HARROW
jobs.tts_text: HALO. Initiate Regional Operational Review, live mode. Reconcile all site data to Regional targets.

jobs.tts_text: STOP! DON'T MOVE! MOVE EVERYTHING! I'm not loading that! I've lost count! CAN I HELP?

jobs.tts_text: The system is now ensuring that reality matches its projections.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: It's going to rewrite the building.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The HALO wall lights up like a slot machine. KPIs cascade across the screen. Trailer assignments rewrite themselves. Labels print uncontrollably from the ceiling vents. jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Cats appear on the conference table. On the HALO wall. On Harrow's tablet. One sits on the "SUBMIT" button.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis has one more resource. A second mint? No. He has a mint's worth of faith in the world being solid. The glow inside him climbs past what the mint was ever meant to hold.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: TOTAL LOGISTICS AWARENESS.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis perceives every pallet. Every trailer. Every serial number. Every destination. Every staging lane. Every production order. Every scanner record. Every misplaced forklift. Every missing manifest. Every cat: all two hundred and fourteen, plus the few who chose to stay.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: It runs through him like a river of freight. For a few seconds, he understands the entire supply chain. It is enormous. It is stupid. It is beautiful.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The HALO wall floods with records, true and false.

jobs.speaker: HARROW
jobs.tts_text: That's not... the dashboard doesn't...

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The false records strike red and vanish, one by one. The true records glow green and settle back into place. The suite goes very quiet.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis turns to the HALO terminal at the side of the table. There is a login. He has a password from somebody who technically doesn't work here, and a crumpled label that has been in his pocket since 9:02.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis remembers he has a bigger task, and puts the scanner away.

jobs.speaker: HARROW
jobs.tts_text: Whatever you are about to do, Hollis, do it.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The terminal waits. Harrow waits. A cat on the table waits, with the most patience.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: ACCESS DENIED. Hollis has no password for this terminal.

jobs.tts_text: Template 000. Tucker printed it by accident. It's the only record HALO never rewrote.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis hesitates. The wall still says 100% about everything. Harrow is watching the wall, not him.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The prompt keeps blinking. The dashboard behind it is still lying. Nothing is fixed until the label goes in.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis pats his pockets. He has nothing the optic reader would recognise as ground truth.

jobs.tts_text: I was managing numbers. I thought the numbers were the warehouse.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: No.

jobs.tts_text: The warehouse never stopped being right. It was just underreported.

jobs.tts_text: She glances at Hollis. Hollis glances at the door.

jobs.tts_text: We're working on it.

jobs.tts_text: It's not.

jobs.tts_text: And Sergeant Biscuit?

jobs.speaker: PRUDENCE
jobs.tts_text: He's got a piece of paper on him. Stuck to his fur. From the trailer. He wears it like a medal. He hangs around Rack 14. He'll do anything for a fish cracker.

jobs.speaker: PRUDENCE
jobs.tts_text: The cats found the warm building and told their friends. Cats are like that. One colony calls the next colony, and the next.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: And when I need him to leave?

jobs.speaker: PRUDENCE
jobs.tts_text: He'll leave for me. Just say when.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Prudence was in the break room?

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: Was she? She's everywhere. Anyway! How can I help? I'm great at helping.

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: HOLLIS! You're awake! I've been so worried! I'm on Inbound, three weeks in, remember? I unload the trailers and put them in the computer! I tried to wake you but Prudence said you needed the sleep.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: I'm mildly proud of how much I'm not mad.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: It's back in my scanner now. Fine.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: It's in the clock. Fine.

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: You're not mad?

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: Oh! The clock kept dying, and I needed a battery that was... shaped like a battery. I found one in a broken scanner in the trash. Was that yours? [nervous] I put tape on it.

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: Oh, it chirped at me. Something scary was behind the vending machine so I told it to stay there. Then I forgot. Sorry! I'm so sorry!

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Tucker, could you un-organize the aisle to staging?

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Yeah.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Tucker picks up the first pallet with the confidence of a man who has never once been told no. The second pallet goes with it. The third goes with both. There is a clatter, a shout, and a tearing sound. From inside a torn box, a small cat emerges, stretches, and walks away.

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: Yes! Absolutely! I love un-organizing! Watch this!

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: The aisle's open, though!

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: Oh no. It was in there.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: You put them in bowls.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Tucker. The cat bowls. Somebody put them out. Nobody's admitting to it.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis makes a mental note: there's a leaking pallet of kibble in staging, labeled "counterweight". The break room, the floor, and staging each have a bowl left. He should collect them.

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: ...It was me. There was a tote in staging leaking little brown pellets. The label said counterweight. It didn't smell like a counterweight. It smelled like a snack. And the cats looked so hungry.

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: Six. Now I see how that might be a problem.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Tucker. I need you to stand at the outbound side door and hold it open. Arms out. Don't move. Don't "help".

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: That is the whole job. It is the most important thing I'll ask of you today.

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: I've never been given an important job with so few steps.

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: That's it? That's the whole job?

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Tucker is not in the cage. Tucker is somewhere else, doing something wonderful and unhelpful.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: The cage key.

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: Hollis! Hi! Isn't this great? I let the cats out of the secured area but the door locked behind me and now I'm the secured area!

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Halvorsen is asking where you are.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Torvald, what did you see?

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: I take my breaks at dawn. Friday, door nine was up. Somebody had cut a trailer seal — 88112 — clean. And the label printer was running with nobody near it.

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: The cats? They've been camping by the drain since spring. Ask Prudence. She'll say she doesn't know. She's lying beautifully.

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: Halvorsen is always asking where people are. Where's that ever gotten him?

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: You found me. Impressive. Tell no one. I'm the dock spotter. I spot. That is the job.

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: Tucker carried a leaking tote from the trailer to staging. Says counterweight. Rattles like kibble. I know kibble. I have a dog. And I have opinions on dogs.

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: I told you everything. I have nothing else. I have a cigarette.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Thanks, Torvald.

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: I already told you. Go bother Prudence.

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: No one thanks Torvald. I like that about you.

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: The drain. Of course. The cats know where I hide. They've always known. They sit near me. Judging. Warm.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Torvald.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: I need to know what you saw Friday at 4:07.

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: Behind stacked equipment. Management has checked here twice. I stood right there both times.

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: You have the log. I have the smoke.

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: You ate a mint, didn't you. You've got the look.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Torvald, I need a spotter at door 3. Trailer's coming in.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: It's brief.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Under ten minutes.

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: How brief?

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: I'll be there. I'll be the guy standing exactly where I'm supposed to be. Don't make it weird.

jobs.speaker: TORVALD
jobs.tts_text: I'm at dock 3 in spirit.

jobs.speaker: RUFUS
jobs.tts_text: Thanks. It's at 147. It's always at 147.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Lost & Found. Under a pink blanket.

jobs.speaker: RUFUS
jobs.tts_text: My clicker. Where was it?

jobs.speaker: RUFUS
jobs.tts_text: I've been counting cats by memory. Do you know how hard that is? I'm at 143. Or 147. It depends when I look.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Rufus pulls a folded, grease-smudged map from his visor. It shows every trailer in the yard, every spot, every row, in thin ink, with dates.

jobs.speaker: RUFUS
jobs.tts_text: Okay. You want to know where the trailers actually are. Not where the WMS thinks. Here.

jobs.speaker: RUFUS
jobs.tts_text: Only in the computer. That's a different place.

jobs.speaker: RUFUS
jobs.tts_text: Not yet. The WMS has that trailer on a compliance hold. If I pull it into door 3, the whole building will yell at me. Soon.

jobs.speaker: RUFUS
jobs.tts_text: The WMS has T-9022 on a hold. If I bring it in without an override, the dock kiosk will lock the door on me. Someone needs to clear it. Maybe someone who's not technically here.

jobs.speaker: RUFUS
jobs.tts_text: I can't see door 3 from the cab. I need a spotter at the dock, someone who knows when it's clear. Torvald is big enough to see over things.

jobs.speaker: RUFUS
jobs.tts_text: Be at the outbound dock. I need to see you. I need the light green. Get there and radio again.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: I've only got

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: on the dock. I need all eight.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: Okay. Let's load.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Bruno slides the jack under the first pallet. Then the second. Torvald calls the dock plate. Tucker holds the door. The cats are somewhere better. One by one, the eight pallets go into the trailer.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: Not until I have a bill of lading, remote confirmation, and Kestrel's okay. [pause] But that looks like a real load. It looks like a load somebody planned.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: Eight loads. One through eight. Nothing on the floor. No cats. Trailer's full and correct.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: That's it.

jobs.speaker: TABITHA
jobs.tts_text: It's brand-new. I wrote it this morning. I'm very proud. It's the first time I've made a policy on the spot. It feels... powerful.

jobs.speaker: TABITHA
jobs.tts_text: Cats are a learning opportunity! With paperwork.

jobs.speaker: TABITHA
jobs.tts_text: Juno has been its most active member in years. She hasn't missed a meeting. Nobody has told her when the meetings are.

jobs.speaker: GUS
jobs.tts_text: Then no. Regional rules. I can't bend those. I'm pretty sure that's the only rule I'm allowed to know.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: I don't have one.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Gus's eyes flick briefly to a monitor showing Rack 14. Then away.

jobs.speaker: GUS
jobs.tts_text: Great. Then it's a loop.

jobs.speaker: GUS
jobs.tts_text: Prudence? I'm aware Prudence is present. Yes. We've all been aware. Security has determined this is an Operations matter.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Operations says it's a Security matter.

jobs.speaker: GUS
jobs.tts_text: I have eight monitors. Six of them have cats on them. I've made my peace.

jobs.speaker: GUS
jobs.tts_text: I didn't say anything about Conveyor 9. I'm not saying anything about the server closet either. That's the sort of thing that wouldn't appear on a monitor I'm watching.

jobs.speaker: GUS
jobs.tts_text: I don't know that word. What word is that?

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Juno did most of it.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Renata and her volunteers walk the ramp. A steady, gentle line of cats climbs into the vans. One by one, they're counted.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Renata looks at Juno, at the armband, at Juno's posture. Juno sits, ears up, tail slow.

jobs.speaker: RENATA
jobs.tts_text: She's a natural. We could use her. [pause] No, you can't give her to us.

jobs.speaker: RENATA
jobs.tts_text: You must be Hollis. I'm Renata. This is the largest colony I've ever been called to. And the best-organized.

jobs.speaker: HOLLIS
jobs.tts_text: Technically no.

jobs.speaker: RENATA
jobs.tts_text: Two hundred and fourteen. Fed, healthy, mostly judgmental. The colony leader, an orange one, walked in like he was reviewing the accommodations. Somebody named them all. Prudence, I'm told. [pause] Is she... employed here?

jobs.speaker: RENATA
jobs.tts_text: The last few, the ones who like the office, can stay if they want. They've got seniority.

jobs.speaker: RENATA
jobs.tts_text: They're all settled. Thank you for the trailer. Really. And the blanket. They love the blanket.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis would call someone, but his phone is in his locker. Somewhere in the locker area is a locker with his name on it, or his initials.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis thumbs through his contacts. The phone reminds him it has 4% battery. It has had 4% for a while.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: I'm four feet from where you were. Come in person. It's cheaper.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: Yes. Is it the shipment? It's always the shipment. Fine. Keep going. Did you check the dashboard? It's green.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis reaches for his radio. It is not there. It is behind the vending machine.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: Yes? Is it the shipment? Fine. Also, if you see cats: they aren't there.

jobs.speaker: HALVORSEN
jobs.tts_text: Status? Give me a number. Any number. I'll take a green one.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: Eight to Kestrel. Right eight. I'm eating lunch.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: Trailer at the door and I'll load. I need to see it. You know where to find me.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: Find me an H-17 seal for this jack, then we talk.

jobs.speaker: BRUNO
jobs.tts_text: Orange dot: mine, ships. Blue dot: stays inside. No dot: I didn't touch it — cat or label. Kestrel's PO tells you the rest.

jobs.speaker: RUFUS
jobs.tts_text: I'd love to talk, but I'm off count without my clicker. It's... somewhere lost.

jobs.speaker: INGRID
jobs.tts_text: Come to my desk. The radio is for emergencies. Everything is a small emergency, but this isn't one.

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: Hollis! You're calling ME? I'm great! What can I help with? I'm holding a pallet. A different one. I'm fine.

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: Hollis! I'm in the cage! It's cozy! The key is in Parts somewhere! Probably!

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: I'm holding the door! I'm not moving! Is it working?

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis sits down at the break-room table. Juno follows him in and settles at his feet. The lights, at long last, stop flickering.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The vending machine makes a noise. It is not a good noise. It is not a bad noise. It is a noise like a thought.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A cat slowly walks into the break room.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis stares at it. Juno stares at Hollis.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: One glowing mint drops into the tray.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A large orange cat, sitting like a sergeant, with a slightly chewed sheet of paper stuck to the fur of his side like a medal. He looks at Hollis with authority and, faintly, hunger.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: CAT — SGT. BISCUIT. Rank: colony leader. Attached document: MANIFEST T-4417, PAGE 2 OF 2. Status: "worn as a medal". Weakness: fish crackers, 80%.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The paper is loosened by a neat sweep of a paw. It slides off his fur and lands at Hollis's feet.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis offers the fish crackers. Sergeant Biscuit sniffs. He considers. He eats one with the dignity of a sommelier.

jobs.speaker: PRUDENCE
jobs.tts_text: Oh, don't. I'm not technically in possession of that.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The trail is already down.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis lays a line of kibble along the main aisle, from the racks toward the outbound dock. It's like leaving breadcrumbs, except for two hundred hungry witnesses.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis slits the stretched wrap. A small waterfall of brown pellets pours out. It smells like fish, tuna, and the entire history of feline temptation. This is not a counterweight.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis has enough kibble. Nobody needs a buffet.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The shrink wrap is committed. Whatever is inside, the pallet is not going to volunteer it.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis grabs the vending machine and pulls. It tilts. It considers. It commits.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis looks at the forklift. The keys are in it. Nobody is watching.

jobs.speaker: TUCKER
jobs.tts_text: Oh thank goodness! I thought I broke it! [pause] I did break it.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The parts gate is locked. Hollis tries the old brass key. It fits like it was cut for a fired employee. Click. He's in.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Juno is not here. Hollis pets the air out of habit.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis pets Juno. Juno accepts this as her due.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis extends a hand toward a cat. The cat considers it, allows exactly two strokes, and then files a complaint with its eyes.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: There is no cat here. It is a strange thing to miss.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Feeding the cats is how this started. Nobody is going to say that out loud, but the narrator is thinking it.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis has never hit anything at work. It is why he is still employed. Mostly.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis considers it. HR, somewhere, sits up in its chair. He does not.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis is tempted. That is how the day started. He stays standing.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis does none of that. He is a professional. He is also very tall, and it would not end well near the racks.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis yells. The warehouse, which has heard everything, has no response. A cat blinks.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis does not smoke. That is Torvald's department, and Torvald would like it to stay that way.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis does not have any coffee. The break room pot smells like a rumor.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: It is the last decent coffee. It is not Hollis's. It has a destination.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis does not have a mint. Yet.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis holds the mint at arm's length. Not yet. Not until it is a real problem.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Nothing happens. Wrong game. The vending machine hums, judgmentally.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis: tall, skinny, cap, gray shirt, blue vest, boots, stubble. He looks like a man who has already seen the incident report.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The game saves itself as you go. The warehouse does not.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis considers quitting. He has considered it since 2019. He is still here.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis swears mildly. A cat looks away, out of courtesy.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis waits. The clock in the break room agrees it is 9:02.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis considers that command. The parser considers Hollis. Neither is moved.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis looks for a way to go there. He does not find one.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis doesn't see that here.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Using a forklift on that is technically a workplace incident. Hollis declines.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis doesn't have that.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The door to the locker area. Beyond it, the sounds of a warehouse having a day.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Back to the break room.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Through the door: the warehouse floor. You can hear it from here.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: HALO WALL SCREEN — Reports: "Everything is fine." Confidence: 100%. Correlation with physical reality: pending since 2021.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The racking aisles, going back further than anyone has surveyed.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: INGRID — Knows: everything. Says: 11%. Owes: nobody. Needs: coffee, CRITICAL.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: HALVORSEN — Stress: CRITICAL. Confidence in dashboard: 91%. Confidence in warehouse: pending. Currently waiting on: a call from someone.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A staircase that leads up to the Regional Operations Suite. A sign at the top: "AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL. NO CATS. See: cats."

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: HR TABLET — Contents: 412 policies. Missing: 1 relevant policy.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: BIN H-17 — HYDRAULIC SEAL KIT x1, last one. Donut: unclassified.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: P-114 — PROPANE SIT-DOWN. System says: PROPANE SIT-DOWN. Correct. P-114 is the one forklift in the building the computer is right about.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The hidden tunnel behind rack 14.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The tunnel ends at a service door marked "SERVER CLOSET — REGIONAL". It is open a crack. A cat is holding it.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: SEAL 88112 — Status: BROKEN. Trailer: T-4417. Time cut: Friday, 4:07 AM. Wait... that's the time the label printer was also printing. Coincidence: rated 3%.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: BUTT BUCKET — 1,204 cigarette butts. Estimated torvald-hours: 61. Note: "management has checked here. Twice. He was not here." Note: "he was."

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: PRUDENCE — Status: TERMINATED / FEEDING. Cats fed: yes. Guilt: no. Hours: 11 weeks.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: GUS — Vigilance: 100%, for the right things. Aware of: Prudence, yes, cats, yes, Conveyor 9, no comment.

jobs.speaker: SCANNER
jobs.tts_text: BADGE READER — Access: REGIONAL. Your access: "hah".

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A scanner battery pack with strips of electrical tape still on it. Held in a clock for who knows how long. It has a little green LED, which is optimistic.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Your cell phone. 4% battery. It has been at 4% since Thursday. It appears to run on stubbornness.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A mug of what may indeed be the last decent coffee in the building. It is hot. It is precious. It should not be wasted on anyone who has not earned it.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A blue pen. It writes. In this building, that alone is a distinction.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A leather work glove the size of a small oven mitt. It smells like pine, tobacco, and a Viking with very little interest in being found.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A pink blanket that has been through some things. It is soft. It has a cat hair on it, which is either a coincidence or a preview.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A hydraulic seal kit for a pallet jack. Small, unloved, and the difference between a working shift and a crawling one.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: An old brass key on a Parts Department lanyard, faded to "PARTS". It came from a person who is technically not authorized to possess it. Presumably she possesses it in a technical sense.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The maintenance cage key. The tag says "IF FOUND SEE TUCKER". Tucker is in the cage. This is the world working as intended.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Bruno's pallet jack, repaired, in your pocket. It is, by any standard, physically impossible to carry in a pocket. The inventory has never asked.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: KESTREL MOTOR WORKS — PO 55-1187 — HOT. Lines: 1) CUSHION-TIRE FORKLIFT ×2, CT-118, CT-119. 2) MAST ASSEMBLY, 3-STAGE. 3) OVERHEAD GUARD KIT. 4) 48V BATTERY PACK. 5) HYDRAULIC HOSE KIT. 6) CONTROL HARNESS CRATE. 7) COUNTERWEIGHT BLOCKS, IRON. That is eight loads. Nothing else. No reach trucks. No tires. No cat food.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A scoop of feline nutrition, bulk grade, in an old tote lid. It smells irresistible to cats and, evidently, to everything with whiskers within a half-mile.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: FORM 9-M: EXEMPTION FOR NON-STANDARD BREATH. "The employee has been informed that no policy exists regarding supernatural breath mints, and is hereby exempt from all policies relating thereto." Signed by Tabitha. Stamped twice.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A small round mint, glowing a soft, confident green-white. It hums, faintly, at a frequency Hollis associates with the fluorescent lights at 9:02. Several company policies prohibit it. None of them name it.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: A grease-stained spiral notebook: "SMOKE LOG". Entries: "FRI 4:07 AM — HALO printer prints by itself. Label kiosk approves own directive. Says 'thank you' out loud. Time: 4:07. Note: nobody was there but me and a cat." Signed: TORVALD. Witness.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: The bill of lading for T-9022: eight loads, correct pallet IDs, correct serials, correct destination, printed by a woman who was told the truth. It is the cleanest piece of paper in the building.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: It is bolted down, in a way that suggests someone else has already tried.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis has taken enough things that were not his today. He declines.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Taking that would create paperwork. Hollis is at capacity.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: It does not open. Or it does, and nothing interesting happens.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Hollis checks. It is as open as it is going to get.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
jobs.tts_text: Pushing it would only relocate the problem.

jobs.speaker: NARRATOR
